m: vīkṣ (vi-√ īkṣ) Ā. vīkṣate (ep. also P.), to look at, see, behold, ŚBr. &c. &c.; to look upon, regard (pitṛ-vat, as a father), R.; (with hṛdi) to see in the heart, ponder, R.; to consider, observe, discern, ascertain, understand, Mn.; MBh. &c.; to think fit or proper, Suśr.; to look over, peruse, study, VarBṛS. : Pass. vīkṣyate, to be looked at &c.; to look like, appear, Vikr.
a: vīkṣ 1 A. 1 To see, behold; taṃ vīkṣya vepathumatī Ku. 5. 85; subhagaṃ tathaiva khalu sāpi vīkṣate V. 4. 3. 2 To regard or consider as.

m: vīrya n. (ifc. f(ā). ) manliness, valour, strength, power, energy, RV. &c. &c.
manly vigour, virility, semen virile, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
a: vīryaṃ [vīr-yat, vīrasya bhāvo yat vā] 1 1 Heroism, prowess, valour; vīryāvadāteṣu kṛtāvamarṣaḥ Ki. 3. 43; R. 2. 4, 3. 62, 11. 72; Ve. 3. 3. 2 Vigour, strength. 3 Virility. 4 Energy, firmness, courage. 5 Power, potency; jāne tapaso vīryaṃ Ś. 3. 2. 6 Efficacy (of medicines); ativīryavatīva bheṣaje bahuralpīyasi dṛśyate guṇaḥ Ki. 2. 4; Ku. 2. 48. 7 Semen virile; Ku. 3. 15; Pt. 4. 50. 8 Splendour, lustre. 9 The seed of plants. 10 Dignity, consequence. Comp. — jaḥ a son. — prapātaḥ seminal effusion, discharge of semen. — śālin a. strong. — hīna a. 1 cowardly, pusilanimouspusillanimous. 2 seedless. 3 impotent.

m: vīrya—vat (vīrya-), mfn. possessing vigour or might, strong, powerful, efficacious, victorious, AV. &c. &c.
vīrya—vat m. N. of a divine being reckoned among the Viśve Devāḥ, MBh.
of a son of the tenth Manu, Hariv.; MārkP.
a: vīryavat a. 1 Strong, stout, vigorous. 2 Efficacious.

m: desired, liked, loved, pleasant, RV.; ŚāṅkhŚr.
vīta n. a wish, desire, TĀr.
the driving or guiding of an elephant (with a goad) &c., Śiś. v, 47.
vīta mfn. gone away, departed, disappeared, vanished, lost (often ibc. = free or exempt from, without, -less), Up.; Mn.; MBh. &c.
vīta mfn. covered, hidden, concealed, RV. (cf. kṛtsna-v˚)
covered or wrapped in, girt with (instr.), ib.; BhP.
vīta mfn. (prob. fr. √ vai; for vīta See under √ vī) worn out, useless, L.
vīta n. a useless horse or elephant, L.
a: vīta p. p. [vi˚i-kta] 1 Gone, disappeared. 2 Gone away, departed. 3 Let go, loosed, set free. 4 Excepted, exempt. 5 Approved, liked. 6 Unfit for war. 7 Tame, quiet. 8 Freed from, devoid of (mostly in comp.); vītaciṃta, vītaspṛha, vītabhī, vītaśaṃka &c. 9 Desired, wished for. 10 Put on or worn — taḥ An elephant or horse unfit or untrained for war. — taṃ Pricking (an elephant) with the goad and striking with the legs; vītavītabhayā nāgāḥ Ku. 6. 39 v. l. (see Malli. thereon); nirdhūtavītamapi bālakamullalaṃtaṃ Śi. 5. 47. Comp. — daṃbha a. humble, lowly. — bhaya a. fearless, intrepid. — (yaḥ) an epithet of Viṣṇu. — mala a. pure. — rāga a. 1 free from desire; Ku. 6. 39 v. l. 2 free from passion. calm, tranquil. 3 colourless. — (gaḥ) 1 a sage who has subdued his passions. 2 a deified Jaina saint. — śokaḥ (= aśokaḥ) the Aśoka tree. — sūtraṃ the sacred thread.

m: vīta—manyu mfn. free from resentment or anger, KaṭhUp.
exempt or free from sorrow, MBh.
vīta—rāga mfn. free from passions or affections, dispassionate, desireless, calm, tranquil, MBh.; Kāv. &c. (also applied to 8 partic. Bodhisattvas and their attributes)
vīta—rāga m. a sage with subdued passions (esp. applied to a Buddhist or Jaina saint), L.
vīta—rāga—bhaya-krodha mfn. free from passions and fear and anger, Bhag.
vīta—śoka mfn. free from sorrow, ŚvetUp.; MBh.
vīta—śoka m. the Aśoka tree, Jonesia Asoka, MBh.
